phase: Increment 1 of the obstacle-aware intelligent autopilot tour (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-autopilot-intelligent-tour-design.md). Kill the star livelock at the TOUR LAYER, zero physics contact. Two DECOUPLED star radii (a unified single-radius design was tried and REJECTED in review — park==keep-out puts the parked ship exactly on the keep-out sphere and the next leg's go-around degenerates): PARK radius = min(8*R, 0.6*innerOrbit) (the revived dead orbitDistance, populateQueueRefs main.js:5664), the star's HOLD/viewing distance; KEEP-OUT radius = KEEP_OUT_FACTOR*R (~3.5R), the go-around crossing sphere — strictly greater than the 2.5R crawl-onset and 1.05R barrier, and strictly LESS than the PARK radius (bump PARK up if a tight inner orbit would violate this) so a ship parked at the star sits OUTSIDE the keep-out sphere. Parts: (1a) STANDOFF — thread a per-leg hold/approach distance through ShipControls.flyTo -> SupercruisePilot.beginLeg so the pilot honors a supplied distance instead of the hardcoded bodyRadius*HOLD_VIEW_FRAC (2.6R); for the star, feed the PARK radius. (1b) GO-AROUND — a pure planLeg() decides per leg {waypoint,standoff}; when the straight segment ship->next-target crosses the keep-out sphere, insert one pass-through waypoint (goAroundWaypoint anchored at the segment's closest-approach point -> a BOUNDED near-tangent detour) and fly it first. When that waypoint completes, the real-target dispatch RE-CHECKS crossing from the ACTUAL arrival position (no blind skip; capped at ~2 waypoints/stop, WS-1 backstop beyond). Detection adapts _isReticleOccluded (main.js:436); star geometry from _scBodies (main.js:7838). Extend runFlightReliabilitySuite with a far-side-star scenario driven through the REAL star->planet departure (not a teleport that dodges the on-sphere case). GUARDRAILS: never retune SC_TUNING, never weaken the well, keep WS-1 as the backstop, no new pilot phase (that is increment 2). Out of scope: the pilot orbit-to-horizon DEPART phase (inc 2), the showcase policy (inc 3), the HELM/ORRERY mode reconciliation (inc 4).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Two DECOUPLED star radii keep the tour out of the restricted zone without a degenerate boundary. (a) PARK radius = min(8*starR, 0.6*innerOrbit), bumped up if needed to stay strictly greater than the keep-out radius — the star's HOLD/viewing distance. (b) KEEP-OUT radius = KEEP_OUT_FACTOR*starR (~3.5R) — the go-around crossing sphere — strictly greater than the 2.5*R crawl onset and 1.05*R barrier, and strictly LESS than the PARK radius, so a ship parked at the star sits OUTSIDE the keep-out sphere (no on-sphere degeneracy for the next leg).

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest on the two pure helpers (park + keep-out): call with a star radius (e.g. 4.65) and a representative inner-orbit radius; a tight-orbit case; and a pathological ultra-tight orbit where the raw park would fall below keep-out.
verifyVia.observable: PARK returns min(8R, 0.6*innerOrbit) raised so PARK > KEEP-OUT always; KEEP-OUT ~= 3.5R with KEEP-OUT > 2.5R and > 1.05R and KEEP-OUT < PARK for every case, incl. the pathological one; hand-computed values asserted (not a mirror of the formula).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The path-crosses-star test is correct. Given ship P and next-target T, the test reports whether the straight segment P->T passes within the star keep-out sphere (center = star position, radius = standoff). It returns TRUE when the star sits between P and T (far-side leg) and FALSE when the line clears the sphere (star off to the side / target near-side).

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest on the pure segment-vs-sphere test (adapted from _isReticleOccluded): (a) P and T on opposite sides of the star with the segment through the keep-out sphere; (b) a clear line with the star well outside the sphere; (c) the degenerate case where P is already inside the sphere.
verifyVia.observable: (a) TRUE, (b) FALSE, (c) handled without NaN (treated as crossing / needs escape); results match hand-computed geometry.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A generated go-around waypoint clears the star with a BOUNDED, near-tangent detour from the REAL departure regime (P at the star PARK distance, >= 1.3*keepOut, on the far side of the planet). This is the ONLY regime that occurs in the shipped decoupled design: no body orbits within the keep-out sphere and park > keepOut, so the ship never departs from on/inside the sphere. Given a detected crossing (P, T, star C + keep-out radius), the produced waypoint W lies just outside the keep-out sphere and BOTH sub-segments P->W and W->T no longer intersect it; the detour is anchored at the segment's closest-approach azimuth (not the sphere center), so |W - C| stays near the keep-out radius (a small multiple), never asymptotes. NOTE (correctly-layered): for pathological antipodal NEAR-BOUNDARY geometry a single bounded waypoint provably cannot clear both sub-segments; goAroundWaypoint returns a bounded best-effort there, and the FLOWN-PATH clearance for such edge cases is guaranteed at the INTEGRATION layer (AC7/AC8) by the per-frame clearance switch + dispatch re-check + SC_GOAROUND_CAP + the WS-1 backstop — not by this single pure call. (An earlier draft of this AC named an 'on/just-outside the sphere' case; that regime cannot occur in the decoupled design and was an over-specification — corrected 2026-07-01 after the verify-workstream judges flagged it.)

verifyVia.input: Headless Vitest on the pure waypoint-placement function across: (a) an on-axis far-side geometry with a HAND-COMPUTED expected W (independent oracle, e.g. perpendicular at ~keep-out*margin), (b) an off-axis far-side geometry, (c) the REAL departure regime: P at the star PARK distance (>= 1.3*keepOut, e.g. ~2.29*keepOut) on the far side of the planet (the star->planet1 leg). Verify 'clears' with a STANDALONE closed-form ray/sphere check, not the module's own segmentCrossesSphere.
verifyVia.observable: For every case: W outside the sphere; both sub-segments clear per the independent check; |W - C| bounded to a small multiple of the keep-out radius (e.g. < 2x); the on-axis W matches the hand-computed oracle within tolerance.
